newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Tuesday.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed today amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. The interbank rate was unchanged and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.90/2.85 percent compared with Monday's yield of 2.95/2.90 percent.
One-year closed at a yield of 2.70/2.65 percent against Monday's yield of 2.72/2.67 percent.

Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.55/98.60 from Monday's close of S$98.53/98.58, September 2001 was unchanged from Monday's close of S$96.35/96.45 and June 2003 ended at S$94.41/94.46 versus S$94.39/94.44.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from Monday's 3-1/2 3-3/8 percent.
